stance_basis: paraphrase states virtually all NPA manufacturers believed the proposed standard level was too high
summary: Domestic manufacturers of NPAs collectively argued that the proposed MY 1979 average fuel economy standard of 18.7 mpg was set too high, citing the fuel economy penalties imposed by emissions standards and other factors. They also raised issues about test procedure changes, California emission standards, weight reduction feasibility, and the need for a separate classification for four-wheel-drive general utility vehicles. Their comments prompted the agency to revise the EIS to cover a range of fuel economy levels and two NPA classes, though not all of their arguments were accepted.
complaint_summary: Virtually all domestic NPA manufacturers who submitted comments believed the proposed 18.7 mpg standard level was too high, given the effects of emissions requirements and other factors, and several also argued that four-wheel-drive general utility vehicles deserved separate classification.
summary_quote: Virtually all manufacturers of nonpassenger automobiles who submitted comments indicated their belief that the level of the standard was too high, in light of the effects of emissions and other factors.
